desc:
This dim tunnel is unfinished and unadorned, the walls still scarred by the
picks of Dwarven miners. Facing the entrance is a huge wooden worktable, made of
a single huge slab of oak, which also serves as a counter. Behind it, in the
distance, bright red and yellow coals glow fiercely under the great smelting
pots. Wood smoke laced with the smells of melted rock and hot metal wafts over
the counter whenever a current of air passes this way.
name: Vig's Shop

desc:
The lowest level of the city begins here, where the houses and parks of the
upper areas give way to business and government. The walls rise up straight and
proud to the ceiling, well above your head, which is covered with an intricate
pattern of stonework. The lines weave in and out and over and under each other,
leading your eyes down the hall until the tracery vanishes out of sight. The
main passage to the upper levels rises upwards and westwards, while a short
corridor going straight west leads to a doorway from which a warm blast of acrid
fumes occasionally issues.
name: Kizdin Crafts

desc:
Here all sorts of pottery is created. On the east wall sit several storage sheds
containing various types of clays. In the centre sit two potter's wheels for
forming plates and bowls and other useful objects. Finally the items are fired
in the kilns along the west wall. To the south is arrayed a selection of toys
made from wood and clay.
name: Craftsmen's Shop

desc:
After a long but gentle decline from the west, the corridor here levels out.
This is the commercial centre of the city, and on either side you see doorways
to offices and workshops. The walls are lined with ornamental columns, and
between each two a simple scene is carved into the wall.
name: Kizdin Crafts

desc:
Here are the offices of those who direct the Dwarves' great work. This is a
long, somewhat narrow room, filled with orderly desks, and more paper than
tools. The light is bright and diffuse. All the tunnelling and digging and
carving is overseen from this room. The design of the caves is a careful match
of the needs of the growing population of the caves with the natural desires of
the stone in which they live.
name: Miners and Architects

desc:
All around you busy Dwarves do the work which keep this city alive. You are
completely surrounded by bustling activity, and the Dwarves pay your sloth no
mind. The passage continues east and west as far as you can see, small cones of
light dwindling off into the distance.
name: Kizdin Crafts

desc:
Here is where the miners of the area leave and pick up various mining tools.
Wooden ore buckets and picks of all sizes adorn both the walls and the floor. It
seems messy, yet the workers you see coming and going seem to know exactly where
everything is.
name: Miner's Supply Room

desc:
This dim tunnel leads deeper down into the mountain. Unlike those to the north
it is unfinished and unadorned, the wall still scarred by the picks of Dwarven
miners, whose activity you can faintly hear to the south.
name: Felak-Azan

desc:
The stolid hall stretches off before you. To the east the decor changes; the
patterns of stonework end, and a wide variety of axes hang upon the walls.
Around you are bearded Dwarves of every description and station. Nobility in
their finery walk quickly east to the King's court, while labourers walk the
same way for a pint of mead in the Khazad Kheled-Baruk. On one side of you a
cart is pulled, stacked high with cloths and thread in a thousand colours, and
behind that comes a mule loaded with pig iron. Anything your hands or stomach or
head needs must surely be close at hand.
name: Kizdin Crafts

desc:
The tunnel here is only dimly lit by lanterns along the wall. This seems to be a
recent excavation, and is as yet unused. To the south you hear the sound of
picks striking stone wafting up from a downward-sloping tunnel.
name: Felak-Azan

desc:
From the pick marks on the walls around you, this passage was purposefully
delved, but it seems to have been abandoned. Several dark lanterns hang from the
walls.
name: Felak-Narag

desc:
All along this passage hang axes. From floor to ceiling, they hang majestically,
testament to times of war and glory long since passed from these proud people.
The axes are of all shapes and sizes, lengths and widths. You can spot legendary
axes, from tales told of heroes long gone, their only link back to the living
world. The axes line the way, separated only by white stones, carved bowl-like
into the wall, emitting a faint glow like muted candle-light into the hall.
Jutting out from the stone walls, two signs appear, one on the north wall and
one on the south, their lettering clear and dark in the stone.
name: Felak Baruk

desc:
Though from the outside this alcove looks simple, from within it grows to a
cavernous size, growing tall into the rock and furnished with many walkways and
terraces. Here, dwarves who have travelled from abroad may claim lodging for the
night, resting their backs on the gentle beds of the inn. The atmosphere is
relaxed, as if the tension from without cannot penetrate its hallowed stone
walls.
name: Khazad-dum Barazinkheled

desc:
All along this passage hang axes. From floor to ceiling, they hang majestically,
testament to times of war and glory long since passed from these proud people.
The axes are of all shapes and sizes, lengths and widths. You can spot legendary
axes, from tales told of heroes long gone, their only link back to the living
world. The axes line the way, separated only by white stones, carved bowl-like
into the wall, emitting a faint glow like muted candle-light into the hall.
name: Felak Baruk

desc:
This giant natural cavern spreads out before you like the workplace of Aule.
Stalactites hang down from the roof, bright gems glowing from their tips,
projecting a kalidescopic light all around you, flickering and dancing on the
walls. Giant stalagmites stand, carved masterfully into statues depicting Mahal
in different poses. Many dwarves are here at all times, resting, standing or
kneeling in prayer or reverence. An ornate altar stands here, dominating the
centre of the hall with its presence.
name: Felak Mahal

desc:
This small chamber slopes down into the mountain. Unlike the rest of the caverns
it is only dimly lit here; some few smoky torches serve to cast a flickering
light over the room. Sarcophagi line the floor. On the paths between them walk a
few Dwarves with bowed heads. Here they remember their loved ones, who walk no
more upon this earth, but sit with their fathers in the halls of waiting until
Mahal calls to them again.
name: The Hall of the Dead

desc:
Here sits the Dwarven king, King Under the Mountain, upon his throne of black
rock. His throne dominates the room, a large hall of black stone streaked with
gold. Suits of armour, shining softly in the light, line the walls and regal
carpets cover the floor. Many Dwarven courtiers move about, performing matters
for the king, who sits here listless, his face thrust deep in thought.
name: Felak Uzbad Khuzdul

desc:
This giant natural cavern spreads out before you like the workplace of Aule.
Stalactites hang down from the roof, bright gems glowing from their tips,
projecting a kaleidoscopic light all around you, flickering and dancing on the
walls. Giant stalagmites stand, carved masterfully into statues depicting Mahal
in different poses. Many dwarves are here at all times, resting, standing or
kneeling in prayer or reverence.
name: Felak Mahal

desc:
This small room is lined with shelves dug into the walls, and filled with
cabinets, desks, and chests filled with all sorts of great tomes, old and
yellowed, but still treasured for their store of knowledge. On every surface is
some scroll or map, wall-hanging or book. Here the records of the Dwarves and
their trials upon Arda are written and stored for future generations. Dwarves
linger here for many an hour, simply sitting and pondering, absorbing the past
as if to give them strength for the future. On a table sits a Khuzdul-Westron
dictionary. On a poster on the wall is the Song of Durin. There is also a family
tree of Durin's folk.
name: Felak Mazarbul

desc:
Light seems to shine from everywhere and nowhere here, illuminating the Dwarven
cavern in an eerie glow. Statues line the way, a testimony to greatness gone,
perhaps hinting at greatness to come. The walls are covered in tapestries of
semi-precious stones, forming rock paintings of Dwarven lords and heros, their
eyes shining rubies, looking at all those who pass beneath them. Their eyes seem
almost living, their glint at once sad and accusing, cold and caring, as if the
souls of the ancient Dwarves glimmered within them.
name: Felak Uzbadul

desc:
Light seems to shine from everywhere and nowhere here, illuminating the Dwarven
cavern in an eerie glow. Statues line the way, a testimony to greatness gone,
perhaps hinting at greatness to come. The walls are covered in tapestries of
semi-precious stones, forming rock paintings of Dwarven lords and heros, their
eyes shining rubies, looking at all those who pass beneath them. Their eyes seem
almost living, their glint at once sad and accusing, cold and caring, as if the
souls of the ancient Dwarves glimmered within them.
name: Felak Uzbadul

desc:
The great hall extends before you, an avenue lined by bright rubies, shining
like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise
and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. Carvings cover the walls,
bas-reliefs of ages long since past, heros long dead, and glory long since faded
from Durin's folk, remembered only in the scarlet glow of the rubies and the
stonework of Dwarven artists. The grim faces of the Dwarves around seem to burn
with determination. Perhaps the Hall of Rubies will ring again with the sounds
of Dwarven triumph. To the south, a sign of black rock, lettered in bright ruby
hangs above a lit alcove. From inside, the sounds of merriment can be heard.
name: Felak Barazinkheled

desc:
The great hall extends before you, an avenue lined by bright rubies, shining
like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise
and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. Carvings cover the walls,
bas-reliefs of ages long since past, heroes long dead, and glory long since
faded from Durin's folk, remembered only in the scarlet glow of the rubies and
the stonework of Dwarven artists. The grim faces of the Dwarves around seem to
burn with determination. Perhaps the Hall of Rubies will ring again with the
sounds of Dwarven triumph. To the south, the Hall of Dwarves can be seen, its
sombre walls rising straight up into the ever-dusk recesses of the chamber.
name: Felak Barazinkheled

desc:
The great hall continues before you, a dazzling crimson spectacle, lined by
bright rubies, shining like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is
smooth, polished by the wise and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. The
grim faces of the Dwarves around seem to burn with determination. Perhaps the
Hall of Rubies will ring again with the sounds of Dwarven triumph. All along
this majestic path lie benches carved from dark stone where Dwarves sit and
watch the world pass by the light of a thousand glittering eyes.
name: Felak Barazinkheled

desc:
The great hall extends before you, an avenue lined by bright rubies, shining
like subterranean roses in the light. The floor is smooth, polished by the wise
and skilful hands of master Dwarven craftsmen. Perhaps the Hall of Rubies will
ring again with the sounds of Dwarven triumph. Here the hall ends in a
carved-out alcove with benches smoothed out of the hewn rock walls. By the light
of the glittering gems, several Dwarves sit and read or just look around them in
awe at the work of their forefathers.
name: Felak Barazinkheled

desc:
The tavern is a high ceilinged room filled with the smoke of pipes and the
laughter of Dwarves at ease. Oval tables, growing out of the stone like
mushrooms, dot the floor, while a counter of pure marble marks the bar. Here, it
seems, all cares are forgotten, and the Dwarves who sit around you seem only
interested in a strong drink, a good meal, and the companionship of friends.
name: Khazad Kheled-Baruk

desc:
You are within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose
ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are
rough, filled with small niches and rocky knobs sticking into the hall. To your
northeast, in the centre of this vast chamber, you can see what appear to be
mountains rising up from the floor. Nearest you is a grey mount, rising up to a
silver peak. Farther north stands one like a tooth tipped with snow; its walls
glowing red in the cavern's light.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
You are within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose
ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are
rough, filled with small niches and protrusions sticking into the hall. Directly
to the north you see a miniature mountain rising high above your head, even
here, deep within the Blue Mountains. It rises quickly, hard grey stone
cunningly crafted by the Dwarves, with a silver peak gleaming in the cave's
light.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
You stand within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose
ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are
rough, filled with small niches and protrusions sticking into the hall. Arrayed
to your northwest are three tall, broad towers, cleverly crafted to look like
mountains. All three are made of hard grey stone, with snowy white peaks. The
sheer sides of the furthest gleam a dull red in the light.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
You stand at the corner of an enormous cavern. It opens to the west and north,
and no end to its greatness can be seen. Just to the northwest there is a dark
pool. Towering over it on three sides are mountainous towers, grey and red and
snowy-capped. Fifty feet or so above you there is a large opening in the south
wall.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
You stand within an enormous cavern which extends beyond your vision and whose
ceiling is lost in darkness. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls are
rough, filled with small niches and rocky knobs sticking into the hall. Just to
the east a vast tower of rock rises from the floor, gleaming a snow- white
silver at its peak. To the northeast stands a mountainous tower with sheer,
dull-red sides. Peeking between them you can just see the white peak of a third
tower.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
The ground slopes gently down to a wide clear pool. The area around you is
rough, except for a small flat surface near the pool, and several comfortable
paths leading away. Several Dwarves peer into the pool, thinking of the twilight
time when the first of their race awoke. They seem to be treating the water with
great reverence, taking care not to touch its surface.
name: Zaram Durinul

desc:
You are at the eastern edge of huge cavern deep within the earth. Just to your
west is a small pool, around which stand several unusually contemplative
Dwarves. Many other Dwarves walk quickly north or south.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
Many Dwarves pass by you here, at the northeastern corner of a gigantic opening
in the mountain. This seems to be a major thoroughfare leading east and south.
To your west are three mountains rising high up into the air. Two you see
clearly, hard grey rock rising slowly up to white towers. Behind them you can
glimpse the peak of a third.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
This is a majestic entranceway to an enormous cavern to the west. From the east
a wide corridor slopes slowly up, with constant width and height, until it
approaches its end. There it abruptly widens, the ceiling rises into shadows and
the path splits into two, separated by a massive statue. Dwarves walk quickly
past you carrying all manner of provisions and crafts, paying little heed to the
majestic sculpture.
name: Kizdin Crafts

desc:
In the shelves that line the walls of this room lie countless devices. They all
seem of a strange, mechanical nature. A great table fills the eastern portion of
the room, and several lamps hang above it. On this table are scattered tumblers
and strange instruments.
name: Locksmith's Shop

desc:
Here within this tower in the shape of a mountain, the skills of survival are
taught to those who would go out into the wild, mastering animals and facing the
dangers of the elements. Even dwarven warriors, with faces hard as stone, know
that their skin can be rent and torn, and that it is important to know how to
bind one's wounds so that one may heal and return later on to battle.
name: Bundushathur

desc:
Inside this tremendous tower of stone, the Dwarven war-masters teach the lessons
of combat to their pupils. All around you, Dwarves spar with each other and with
straw dummies, lunging, parrying and swinging their weapons in a synchronized
dance of death. You are surprised at how crowded the sparring area is, and
wonder if the Dwarven armies will once more march against evil in the lands of
Arda.
name: Barazinbar

desc:
You stand at the curved corner of an enormous cavern which extends beyond your
vision to the south and east. Though the floor is perfectly smooth, the walls
are rough, filled with small niches and knobby rocks jutting into the hall. To
the east a great tower rises before you, a mighty peak tipped with snow like
silver, but with sheer naked sides, dull red as if stained with blood. With your
back to the cavern's wall, gazing up at the peak, you can almost believe that
you are far away, and that the Dwarves still live in comfort and prosperity.
name: Gabil Felak

desc:
Standing on the second level of Barazinbar, you behold the war library of the
Dwarves. Shelves and shelves surround you containing countless scrolls and books
detailing Dwarven battle plans and tactics. Many a Dwarven student of war has
spent long hours studying the battles of the Dwarves of old, paying reverence to
those who died to protect their families.
name: Barazinbar Mazurbul

desc:
This is a great circular pit carved in the native stone of the mountains. A
great staircase, wide enough for twenty dwarves to walk abreast, rises gradually
upward, turning counter-clockwise as it goes. Its risers are paved with marble,
and black onyx sconces on the wall hold lamps which are continually filled from
an unseen source and kept burning.
name: Base of a Spiral Staircase

desc:
This large room is wide enough for an enormous wooden table and a dozen or so
chairs. The table itself is piled with papers, which appear to be mainly maps
and city plans for new excavations and mining. A small shelf stands beside the
table with rolls of paper neatly tucked away. Most likely the plans, plats and
copies of deeds of finished homes currently in use.
name: Deeds and Digging Office

desc:
There is a small stretch of apartments here, in a passage between two large
caverns. To the west the rows of Dwarven doorways abruptly ends where a new
tunnel is being delved.
name: Dum Khazdul

desc:
To the west one can see a small wooden structure, where the guards loyal to the
Emissary of Durin's House can take turns to rest. The well-worn stone floor
leads to a roomy hall to the north. To the south the bulky metal-plated wooden
gate protects the entrance.
name: The Entrance of the Emissary of Durin's House

desc:
This hall is one of the greatest achievements of modern masonry, perhaps not
comparable to the great works of Khazad-dum, but still magnificent. In the
center an old table with 24 chairs around it waits to host the next feast. Shiny
metal in the ceiling together with the numerous torches create the illusion of
stars in the sky.
name: The Great Hall

desc:
This looks like a fine place to end the hard day of a military leader and start
a well deserved rest. A door is complemented with woolen cloth to make it
soundproof. A simple but comfortable bed waits for its master.
name: The Emissary's Retreat

desc:
This great hall, unlike others, is not a monument to heros, nor a testimony to
the greatness of kings long buried. It is a hall for all Dwarves, a great cavern
dedicated to the honor of every Dwarf, great or meek, living or dead. The avenue
is lined with trees of stone, trees from whose boughs hang flowers or fruit
carved from fine opals, sapphires, diamonds, and other jewels. The walls are not
covered in reliefs, nor molded by carvings. In fact, they seem utterly bare
until you look closer. Slowly your eyes focus on the marks impressed upon the
stone: names. The name of every Dwarf living and dead is here, to be honored by
all, and remembered.
name: Felak Khazad

desc:
Here the miners have come upon a natural opening in the rock. The floors have
been polished smooth recently, and the walls bedecked with paintings and some
tapestries, in preparation of new Dwarven Homes.
name: Felak-Azan

desc:
Lamps mounted on the smooth stone walls cast flickering shadows around this
well-lit hall. Every surface is impeccably clean, and polished to a shine. The
three columns along the north wall, and the three columns along the south wall
each depict one of the nameless six Dwarven fathers. Above the eastern doorway
the seventh Dwarven father, Durin the first, the deathless, king of Khazad-dum
is shown wearing a crown of seven stars. In the centre of the room rests a
massive stone table around which visitors to Fenuln's hall can gather and feast.
name: Fenuln's Hall

desc:
The walls of this bedroom are rough cut granite with patches of green malachite
carefully exposed, but still embedded in the walls where the water dripping
through the copper rich stone naturally deposited the mineral. Between the large
black bear fur covering the floor and the roaring fireplace, the chamber is
quite cosy. The room is exceptionally well ventilated as there is barely any
scent of smoke from the fire, and a gentle breeze of fresh air can be felt. In
the corner a stone staircase leads downwards.
name: Malachite Bedroom

desc:
Though Dwarves by their nature are not drawn to stealth, some skills have found
their way into Dwarven usage. Here, within mighty Zirakzigil many Dwarves hone
these skills, trained by formidable rogue-captains. Though the Dwarves refuse
such skills as backstabbing, all manner of other rogue skills you see practiced
here.
name: Zirakzigil

desc:
Here, upon the second level of Zirak, all the accumulated Dwarven knowledge of
the scouts' skills is stored. Dwarves flit in and out, reading scroll after
scroll, book after book, detailing how to perform each act of stealth. You are
never quite sure how many Dwarves are in this chamber with you, and you wonder
how many are lurking hidden, unnoticed by your eyes.
name: Zirakzigil Mazurbul
